section: Accidental Deaths and Suicides in India 1977
title: 8 ## Causes of Accidental Deaths: The total accidental deaths reported during 1977 have been classified under two broad categories: (A) accidental deaths due to natural causes, like lightning, heat stroke, landslide etc. and (B) accidental deaths due to other causes, like mishaps in factories, railway accidents, air crashes etc. Category 'A' accounted for 10.1 per cent of total accidental deaths recorded in 1977 in comparison to 3.6 per cent in 1976. Under this category, the maximum number of deaths was reported by Cyclone (8014) followed by 'Lightning' (175.5) 'Floods' (755), 'Landslides' (563), 'Cold and Exposure' (394) and Heat strokes' (363), Category 'B' claimed 89.9 per cent of the total accidental deaths registered during 1977. In 1976, this category had claimed 96.4 per cent of the total accidental deaths. Under this category the maximum number of deaths were recorded under the head 'Drowning' (24946) followed by accidents 'on Roads' (15090), deaths due to 'Fire' (10878), 'Railways' (10207), 'Poisoning' (6666), 'Animal biting/killing' (3522), 'Fire Arms' (1268), 'House Collapse' (1256), 'Mines & Quarry disaster' (748), 'Boat capize'
